findings.highlight: memorable day of when Shirou finally became mine
findings.evidenceJa: シロウがわたしのものになった記念日
findings.governingReading: Illya celebrates the commemorative anniversary or occasion of Shirou becoming hers.
findings.explanation: Memorable day of when is grammatically malformed and adds “finally.”

findings.highlight: We won’t congratulate you, you devil child
findings.evidenceJa: 迎えるかこの悪魔っ子
findings.governingReading: After first joining the applause, Taiga snaps that she will not welcome or receive this little devil that way.
findings.explanation: Congratulate breaks the callback to Illya’s repeated 迎えて invitation to welcome her with applause.

findings.highlight: because you made Shirou yours by force
findings.evidenceJa: 士郎ヘルめぐりの案内人役
findings.governingReading: Taiga refers to Illya’s earlier complaint that she kept serving as Shirou’s guide through hell.
findings.explanation: The English conditionally substitutes an unsupported line about taking Shirou by force.

findings.evidenceJa: 自分でうんって言った
findings.governingReading: Illya deflects blame because Shirou himself said yes, a joke resting on the coercive branch’s false consent.
findings.explanation: Willingly upgrades the bare fact of his spoken assent into genuine voluntary consent and blunts the joke’s cruelty.

findings.governingReading: Taiga mock-grandly calls the four-person arrangement a vague “Paraiso,” using an archaic loanword.
findings.explanation: Ordinary paradise removes the deliberately exotic, old-fashioned comic register.

findings.governingReading: Taiga calls being kept by an underage princess aesthetically decadent in an exaggerated, affected way.
findings.explanation: Beautiful and good is childishly generic and loses the decadent-aesthetic joke.

findings.evidenceJa: タイガやリンやサクラ
findings.governingReading: Illya boasts that this privilege is impossible for Taiga, Rin, or Sakura.
findings.explanation: The English names Taiga and Sakura but omits Rin from the comparison.

findings.governingReading: Rin says, tersely, that the idea was rejected or cut.
findings.explanation: The English conditionally inserts a specific H-scene reference absent from the bound Japanese line.

findings.governingReading: Rin dismisses Illya with the visual insult “bloomers.”
findings.explanation: Buruma leaves the Japanese loanword unexplained in otherwise English dialogue, obscuring the costume gag.

findings.governingReading: Taiga calls Illya her number-one or foremost pupil.
findings.explanation: Senior student changes rank by favor into seniority.

findings.governingReading: In rough pupil speech, Illya says she is fired up or has regained fighting spirit.
findings.explanation: It filled me with spirit is unnatural and makes an unspecified external thing act on her.

findings.highlight: more of a relationship of mutual trust than master and student do
findings.evidenceJa: 師匠以上に信頼関係を築かれている
findings.governingReading: Taiga complains that Illya and Rin seem to have built more trust than Illya has with her own master, Taiga.
findings.explanation: The English turns the pointed personal comparison into a general comparison between relationship types.

findings.highlight: I hate scary stories and horse racing stories
findings.governingReading: Taiga abruptly declares in mock-samurai diction that she detests scary stories and horse-racing stories.
findings.explanation: The English preserves the odd pairing but removes the faux-archaic punchline.

findings.governingReading: Illya assures Taiga that the object is merely a stuffed toy.
findings.explanation: Normal adds a claim about its ordinary nature beyond the source’s narrower “merely.”
